# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 68 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 48 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_068_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 68

**1** Jesus said: "Blessed are you when you are hated and persecuted.

**2** And no place will be found where you have been persecuted."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** The second clause is one of the most puzzling in Thomas. Three interpretations have been proposed: (1) the persecution leaves no permanent trace — it is overcome; (2) the persecuted one transcends worldly location entirely; (3) textual corruption or ellipsis — a line may be missing.

**"No place will be found"** — SOPHIA preserves the enigma without explanation, consistent with Thomas's style of unresolved paradox. PNEUMA's "for" imports a causal reading not in the Coptic; it is an interpretation, not a translation.

**Synoptic Parallels:** The saying is a shortened version of the Q beatitude (Matt 5:10-12; Luke 6:22-23), but the unique second clause is distinctively Thomasine and without canonical parallel.
